definitions.explanation: The quality of being morally right, logically justified, or socially acceptable. Often used when questioning or asserting whether an action, decision, or claim is properly grounded.

examples.japanese: {正当性|せいとうせい}を{主張|しゅちょう}する。
その{決定|けってい}の{正当性|せいとうせい}が{問|と}われている。
examples.english: The legitimacy of that decision is being questioned.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{行動|こうどう}に{正当性|せいとうせい}があると{信|しん}じているからこそ、{強|つよ}く{主張|しゅちょう}できる。
examples.english: It is precisely because you believe your actions are justified that you can argue your case confidently.

notes:
Formed from {正当|せいとう} (legitimate, justified) + {性|せい} (-ness). Used in formal and academic discourse to discuss whether actions or claims are morally or logically sound.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正当性|せいとうせい}を{問|と}う — to question the legitimacy of
- {正当性|せいとうせい}を{証明|しょうめい}する — to prove justification
- {正当性|せいとうせい}を{欠|か}く — to lack legitimacy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {妥当性|だとうせい}: validity, reasonableness (whether something is sensible/appropriate)
- {合法性|ごうほうせい}: legality (whether something is permitted by law)
- {正統性|せいとうせい}: legitimate succession (same pronunciation; refers to rightful authority by lineage or tradition)
